newsitem.title: CHINA: China oil output 156.45 mln tonnes in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China oil output 156.45 mln tonnes in 1996.

text.p: China produced a record 156.45 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, up 8.0 million tonnes from the year before, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
It quoted Zhou Yongkang, president of the state-run China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC), as saying onshore oil output reached 141.41 million tonnes.
The output figures reported by CNPC were close to previously announced estimates.
Onshore natural gas output hit a record 16.44 billion cubic metres in 1996, Xinhua said but gave no comparative figures.

Long-established oil fields in China's eastern regions accounted for 80 percent of national crude oil output and were able to stabilise production and enhance their crude extraction rates through steady exploration and development, it said.

China's largest oilfield, Daqing in the northeastern province of Heilongjiang, produced 56 million tonnes of oil in 1996. Shengli, the second largest oilfield, pumped 29.1 million tonnes, while Liaohe, the third, pumped out 15 million tonnes, it said.

Oil output in western regions, where the three oil-bearing basins of Tarim, Turpan-Hami and Junggar are located, reported strong results, with total oil output hitting 15.4 million tonnes, up 2.56 million tonnes from 1995, the agency said.
CNPC had signed 30 contracts with foreign oil companies in 1996, covering a total contracted area of 206,000 square km, Xinhua quoted Zhou as saying.
He repeated previous estimates for total output this year, saying production was expected to hit 165-167 million tonnes, up 4.2 to 4.5 percent compared with 1996, Xinhua said.
